issue.title: Add test coverage for the fix  RESTEasy Reactive Client: propagate declared exceptions #48291
issue.body:
### Summary

This PR adds test coverage for the fix implemented in https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/48291

Original issue: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/48286

With versions previous to the fix test will fail, for instance, if you execute:
` mvn clean verify -Dit.test=CheckedExceptionWithInterceptorIT -Dreruns=0 -Dquarkus.platform.version=3.19.3`

body:
The scenario being tested is very much an edge case as you are getting a `Uni<Response>` from the client passing it on as the response of the server, while on the event loop. 
I understand what you are trying to do, but I want to think about it a little more

issue.title: Revert the previous handling of Uni<Response> in REST Client
issue.body:
Although this is an edge case, we should probably ensure that it continues to work.

- Closes: #48886
- Follows up on: #48807

body:
Since my update from version 3.24.1 to 3.25.0 I see a similar problem, but I am not using Mutiny return types. My setup is a simple as the following:

```
        final AttachmentDTO attachment = attachmentClient.uploadReceipt(request.getAttachment());
        final Response attachmentData = attachmentsClient.attachments().download(attachment.getId());
        final InputStream streamData = attachmentData.readEntity(InputStream.class);
        final ParseReceiptMultipartFormDTO payload = new ParseReceiptMultipartFormDTO();
        payload.setReceipt(streamData);
        final ReceiptDTO receipt = parseClient.receipts().parse(payload);
```

On Quarkus 3.24.1, this is working fine and I get a response within `receipt`, but when updating to 2.25.0, the very same code throws the following exception on the `parseClient.receipts().parse(payload)` line (see below).

I tried already several different things, adding annotations (@Blocking, @Nonblocking, etc.), wrap it in reactive behavior, changing the client to return Uni. Nothing of this worked.

Not sure if it fits into this issue.
